 RG3 expected to interview for Baylor head coaching job, sources tell ESPN 
 FILE -Former NFL quarterback and current sports commentator, Robert Griffin III, on the field before an NCAA football game between Colorado and TCU on Oct. 4, 2025, in Fort Worth, Texas. (AP Photo/Mike Buscher), File) (Mike Buscher | AP) By Ashley Pinson Published : Nov. 13, 2026 at 11:30 AM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WACO, Texas (KWTX) — Former Baylor quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Robert Griffin III is expected to interview for the Bears’ head football coaching job, sources told ESPN.
 The Copperas Cove High School graduate has publicly expressed interest in coaching at his alma mater, according to ESPN’s report . ESPN noted that On3 first reported news of the expected interview.
 During an Oct. 26 interview on “The Dan Patrick Show,” Griffin said he had spoken with Baylor Athletic Director Doug McNamee about the opportunity following Dave Aranda’s dismissal, ESPN reported. Griffin then confirmed that he was “100%” interested in the job.
 Griffin played for Baylor from 2008 to 2011 and won the Heisman Trophy after leading the Bears to a 10-3 record in his final season, ESPN reported. He later played in the NFL and is now a broadcaster for Fox Sports.
 Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman has been serving as interim head coach since Aranda’s departure. The Bears are 6-3, including wins over UCF and Iowa State under Klanderman, ESPN reported.
 The report says Griffin is expected to interview; it does not say an interview has taken place or that Baylor has selected its next coach.
